newsitem.title: UK: Wolseley says strong pound to hit results.
newsitem.headline: Wolseley says strong pound to hit results.

text.p: International building supplies group Wolseley Plc announced a 12 percent rise in first-half profits on Tuesday but warned that its results for the rest of the year would be hit by the recent strength in sterling.
"For the group as a whole, continued weakness of overseas currencies against sterling will have an adverse impact on second-half results," chairman Richard Ireland said in his results statement.
The company earlier reported that first-half pretax profits for the six months to January 31 rose 12 percent to 124.3 million pounds on sales up 9.8 percent at 2.28 billion pounds.
The interim dividend was increased to 3.3 pence from 3.1 pence on earnings up nine percent at 14.63p a share.
But the plumbing supplies specialist gave a cautious outlook for current trading conditions.

Ireland warned that the management saw little change in conditions in British and mainland European markets for the rest of the year while 12 months of strong growth in its all-important U.S. business was now likely to level off.
British markets were only picking up slowly and little relief could be expected this financial year from depressed economic conditions in its mainland European markets in France and Austria.

"The upturn in the UK housing market remains fragile and is unlikely to deliver much benefit to our UK distribution activities until later in the year," he said. "Consumers may be reluctant to increase expenditure to any great extent until after the election (on May 1)."

The U.S. distribution business, Wolseley's biggest market, proved buoyant in the first half, with trading profits up 21.7 percent at 56.6 million pounds on a 14.6 percent increase in sales to 1.2 billion pounds. Like-for-like sales in U.S. distribution before acquisitions were up 10.3 percent and profits up 16.1 percent.

But Ireland warned that housebuilding starts in the U.S. had slowed recently and it was likely that the rate of growth would slow during the second half relative to the upturn in the equivalent period last year. Against this background the company would be looking for growth in the medium term. "Opportunities should arise...both from the existing businesses and through acquisitions," Ireland said. "The modest gearing ratio provides ample flexibility in this respect," he added. Net borrowings at the end of January stood at 109.6 million pounds, up 49.8 million pounds on a year ago, to give a debt to equity gearing of 13.3 percent.
